brief: Inputs, paths, and the toolchain used to compile them
details: These options tell Mr.Docs which sources to read, where to write the result, and how to compile the code. They cover the command-line inputs and configuration file, the source root and output location, the compilation database, and the include paths, preprocessor defines, and standard-library and toolchain settings the compiler needs to parse the sources.

options.name: cmd-line-inputs
options.details: Positional inputs that drive the run. Each path is dispatched by file name: an input ending in `mrdocs.yml` is read as a configuration file, and an input ending in `compile_commands.json` or `CMakeLists.txt` is read as a compilation database. The dispatch is a convenience; prefer the explicit `config` and `compilation-database` flags so the invocation is unambiguous and easier to read in scripts and CI logs.

options.name: config
options.details: A YAML file holding the options for the run: the source code, the output directory, the compilation database, the generator, and the filters. MrDocs reads it and applies the options it finds.

options.name: source-root
options.brief: Path to the root directory of the source code
options.details: The root directory of the source tree. It is the default location for input files and the base for the relative paths MrDocs forms from absolute ones. Set it to the root of the git project so those relative paths can link back to the source files in the repository; templates build those links from the `base-url` option.

options.name: compilation-database
options.details: The path to a compilation database, or to a build script that generates one. A compilation database is a JSON file of the compiler commands that build the source; MrDocs reads the compiler flags and source files from it to extract symbols. You can also pass a build script such as `CMakeLists.txt`: MrDocs then looks for CMake on `PATH` or in `CMAKE_ROOT`, runs the script, and uses the database it produces.

options.name: cmake
options.brief: CMake arguments when generating the compilation database from CMakeLists.txt
options.details: When the compilation-database option is a CMakeLists.txt file, these arguments are passed to the cmake command to generate the compilation_database.json.

options.name: defines
options.brief: Additional defines passed to the compiler
options.details: Additional defines passed to the compiler when building the source code. These defines are added to the compilation database regardless of the strategy to generate it.

options.name: use-system-stdlib
options.brief: Use the system C++ standard library
options.details: To achieve reproducible results, MrDocs bundles the LibC++ headers. To use the C++ standard library available in the system instead, set this option to true.

options.name: stdlib-includes
options.details: When `use-system-stdlib` is disabled, the C++ standard library headers are available in these paths.

options.name: use-system-libc
options.brief: Use the system C standard library
options.details: To achieve reproducible results, MrDocs bundles the LibC headers with its definitions. To use the C standard library available in the system instead, set this option to true.

options.name: libc-includes
options.details: When `use-system-libc` is disabled, the C standard library headers are available in these paths.

options.name: system-includes
options.details: Directories added to the system header search path. Headers found there are treated as system headers: they come from outside the project and are not checked for warnings or errors. The standard library and other external headers usually live here.

options.name: includes
options.details: Directories added to the header search path. Headers found there are part of the project and are checked for warnings and errors. Reach for this option when MrDocs cannot find a header your code includes.

brief: Which symbols are documented, and which are hidden
details: These options decide which symbols enter the documentation corpus and how the ones that do appear. They filter by qualified name, by category (private members, undocumented declarations, friends, anonymous namespaces, and so on), by location on disk, and by marking specific symbols as private without dropping them from the corpus.

options.name: input
options.brief: Input directories to extract symbols from
options.details: Input directories to extract. Only symbols defined in files in these directories are extracted. The paths are relative to the mrdocs configuration file.

options.name: recursive
options.details: Recursively include files. When set to true, Mr.Docs includes files in subdirectories of the input directories. When set to false, Mr.Docs includes only the files in the input directories.

options.name: file-patterns
options.details: Only files whose names match these glob patterns are extracted. The patterns are relative to the input directories.

options.name: exclude
options.details: Symbols defined in files in these directories are not extracted even if they are in the list of include directories. When relative, the paths are relative to the directory of the mrdocs configuration file. For instance, "include/experimental" will exclude all files in the directory `<config-dir>/include/experimental`.

options.name: exclude-patterns
options.details: Files matching these glob patterns are skipped, even when they sit inside an included directory. The patterns are relative to the configuration file. A single `*` matches everything in a directory; `**` matches everything in a directory and its subdirectories.

options.name: include-symbols
options.details: If any patterns are defined here, only symbols that match one of these patterns are extracted. The patterns are applied to the fully qualified name of the symbol without any leading "::". A single "*" will match all symbols in the namespace. Double "**" will match all symbols in the namespace and its subnamespaces. The patterns also support "?" for any chars, "[<chars>]" for charsets, "[^<chars>]" for inverted charsets, and "{<glob>,...}" for alternatives.

options.name: exclude-symbols
options.details: A symbol that matches one of these patterns is not extracted even if whitelisted by "include-symbols". See the documentation for "include-symbols" for the pattern syntax.

options.name: see-below
options.details: Symbols matching these filters, and symbols in scopes that match, are tagged "see-below" in the documentation. Use it for symbols that belong to the project's private API but that users still interact with. On such a symbol's page the implementation synopsis is rendered as "see-below" and the members of a scope, such as a namespace or record, are not listed, while the rest of the documentation appears as usual. See `include-symbols` for the pattern syntax.

options.name: implementation-defined
options.details: Symbols matching these filters, and symbols in scopes that match, are tagged "implementation-defined". Use it for symbols that belong to the project's private API. An "implementation-defined" symbol has no page of its own, and any reference to it renders as "implementation-defined". See `include-symbols` for the pattern syntax.

options.name: auto-function-objects
options.details: When true, Mr.Docs automatically detects algorithm function objects (informally known as niebloids): variables whose type is a record whose only public non-special members are operator() overloads. Set to false to disable auto-detection and rely solely on the @functionobject/@functor doc command. The @functionobject command is still useful when auto-detection is enabled, to force treatment of types that fail auto-detection (e.g. because they have extra public members); it may be placed on the variable or on the function-object record. When a variable is treated as an algorithm function object, its documentation comes from the record's operator() overloads, falling back to the variable's own doc comment when operator() is undocumented; the record's own doc comment is not used.

options.name: extract-all
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs extracts all symbols from the source code, even if no documentation is provided. MrDocs can only identify whether a symbol is ultimated documented after extracting information from all translation units. For this reason, when this option is set to `false`, it's still recommendable to provide file and symbol filters so that only the desired symbols are traversed and stored by MrDocs.

options.name: extract-private
options.brief: Extraction policy for private class members
options.details: Determine whether private class members should be extracted

options.name: extract-private-virtual
options.brief: Extraction policy for private virtual methods of a class
options.details: Determine whether private virtual methods of a class should be extracted

options.name: extract-private-bases
options.brief: Extraction policy for private base classes
options.details: Determine whether private base classes should be extracted

options.name: extract-static
options.brief: Extraction policy for static members of a file
options.details: Determine whether static members of a file should be extracted. This option does not refer to static members of a class.

options.name: extract-local-classes
options.brief: Extraction policy for records defined locally in source files
options.details: Determine whether records only defined locally in source files should be extracted.

options.name: extract-anonymous-namespaces
options.details: Determine whether symbols in anonymous namespaces should be extracted.

options.name: extract-empty-namespaces
options.details: Determine whether empty namespaces without documentation should be extracted.

options.name: extract-implicit-specializations
options.brief: Implicit template specializations used as base classes are extracted as dependencies
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs extracts implicit template specializations that appear as base classes, treating them as dependencies. This gives it the metadata it needs to resolve the derived class's inherited members, as controlled by the `inherit-base-members` option.

options.name: extract-friends
options.brief: Extraction policy for friend functions and classes
options.details: Determine whether friend functions and classes should be extracted. When set to `true`, MrDocs extracts friend functions and classes. When set to `false`, friend functions and classes are not extracted.

brief: How extracted symbols are arranged and what MrDocs infers from them
details: These options control how the documentation set is presented once the filters have decided what enters it: which inherited members are shown on a class page, the order members appear in, how related declarations are grouped (overload sets, SFINAE expressions, function objects), what MrDocs infers from doc comments (briefs, relations, function metadata), and tolerance for headers the compiler cannot find.

options.name: inherit-base-members
options.brief: Determine how derived classes inherit base members
options.details: Determine how derived classes inherit members of base classes. When set to `never`, derived classes do not inherit members of base classes and only the relationship is stored. When set to `reference`, derived classes list members of base classes but references are still linked to the base class. When set to `copy-dependencies`, a reference is created by default and a copy is created when the base class is a dependency. When set to `copy-all`, a copy is created for each base symbol as if it was declared in the derived class. If the base class is a dependency, the extraction mode is copied from the new parent.

options.name: sort-members
options.brief: Sort the members of a record
options.details: When set to `true`, sort the members of a record by the criterion determined in the `sort-members-by` option. When set to `false`, the members are included in the declaration order they are extracted.

options.name: sort-members-by
options.brief: Determine how members of a record are sorted
options.details: If `sort-members` is set to `true`, determine how members of a record are sorted. When set to `name`, members are sorted by name. When set to `location`, members are sorted by their primary location in the source code, considering the short name of the path and the location in the file.

options.name: sort-namespace-members-by
options.brief: Determine how members of a namespace are sorted
options.details: Although members of namespaces are always sorted, determine how members of a namespace are sorted. When set to `name`, members are sorted by name. When set to `location`, members are sorted by their primary location in the source code, considering the short name of the path and the location in the file.

options.name: sort-members-ctors-1st
options.details: When set to `true`, constructors are sorted first in the list of members of a record.

options.name: sort-members-dtors-1st
options.details: When set to `true`, destructors are sorted first in the list of members of a record.

options.name: sort-members-assignment-1st
options.details: When set to `true`, assignment operators are sorted first in the list of members of a record.

options.name: sort-members-conversion-last
options.details: When set to `true`, conversion operators are sorted last in the list of members of a record or namespace.

options.name: sort-members-relational-last
options.details: When set to `true`, relational operators are sorted last in the list of members of a record or namespace.

options.name: sfinae
options.details: When set to true, MrDocs detects SFINAE expressions in the source code and extracts them as part of the documentation. Expressions such as `std::enable_if<...>` are detected, removed, and documented as a requirement. MrDocs uses an algorithm that extracts SFINAE infomation from types by identifying inspecting the primary template and specializations to detect the result type and the controlling expressions in a specialization.

options.name: overloads
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs detects function overloads and groups them as a single symbol type. The documentation for this new symbol comes from the union of non-ambiguous metadata from the functions.

options.name: missing-include-prefixes
options.brief: Include path prefixes allowed to be missing
options.details: Specifies path prefixes for include files that, if missing, will not cause documentation generation to fail. Missing files with these prefixes are served as empty files from an in-memory file system, allowing processing to continue. For example, use "llvm/" to forgive all includes from LLVM. If any such path is specified, MrDocs will attempt to synthesize missing included types. Only simple sets of non-conflicting inferred types can be synthesized. For more complex types or for better control, provide a shim using the "missing-include-shims" option.

options.name: missing-include-shims
options.brief: Shims for forgiven missing include files
options.details: Specifies a map of include file paths to shim contents. If a missing include file matches a forgiven prefix, MrDocs will use the shim content from this map as the file contents. If no shim is provided for a forgiven file, an empty file is used by default.

options.name: auto-brief
options.brief: Use the first line of the comment as the brief
options.details: When set to `true`, Mr.Docs uses the first line (until the first dot, question mark, or exclamation mark) of the comment as the brief of the symbol. When set to `false`, a explicit @brief command is required.

options.name: auto-relates
options.details: When set to `true`, Mr.Docs automatically finds non-member functions that are related to the current class.

options.name: auto-function-metadata
options.brief: Automatically provide missing documentation for special functions and trivial metadata
options.details: When set to `true`, Mr.Docs automatically provides documentation for special functions, such as constructors, destructors, and operators. It also provides documentation for missing documentation metadata, such as known types.

brief: Generators to create the documentation and their options

options.name: output
options.brief: Directory or file for generating output
options.details: Multipage generators expect a directory. Single page generators expect a file or a directory where the file will be created. If the directory does not exist, it will be created.

options.name: generator
options.brief: Generator used to create the documentation
options.details: The generator is responsible for creating the documentation from the extracted symbols. The generator uses the extracted symbols and the templates to create the documentation. The built-in generators include `adoc`, `html`, and `xml`; data-driven generators can be added by dropping a template folder under <addon>/generator/<name>/.

options.name: multipage
options.details: Generates a multipage documentation. The output directory must be a directory. This option acts as a hint to the generator to create a multipage documentation. Whether the hint is followed or not depends on the generator.

options.name: base-url
options.brief: Base URL for links to source code
options.details: The prefix for links to the source code. MrDocs joins it with the path of each source file to build the link.

options.name: addons
options.details: The directory of template files the generators use to build the documentation. Leave it unset to use the defaults that ship at `share/mrdocs/addons` in the MrDocs installation. To customize the output, copy those defaults to your own directory and point this option at it.

options.name: addons-supplemental
options.brief: Additional addons layered on top of the base addons
options.details: Optional list of supplemental addons directories that are loaded after the base addons (built-in or replacement). Files in later supplemental directories override files from earlier ones and from the base addons. Use this to add or override a few templates/helpers without copying the entire addons tree.

options.name: tagfile
options.details: Specifies the full path (filename) where the generated tagfile should be saved. If left empty, no tagfile will be generated.

options.name: legible-names
options.details: Use legible names for ids in the documentation. When set to true, MrDocs uses legible names for symbols in the documentation. These are symbols that are legible but still safe for URLs. When the option is set to false, MrDocs uses a hash of the symbol ID.

options.name: embedded
options.details: Output an embeddable document, which excludes the header, the footer, and everything outside the body of the document. This option is useful for producing documents that can be inserted into an external template.

options.name: show-namespaces
options.brief: Show namespace pages in the documentation
options.details: When set to true, MrDocs creates a page for each namespace in the documentation.

options.name: show-enum-constants
options.brief: Show enum constant pages in the documentation
options.details: When set to true, MrDocs creates a page for each enum constant in the documentation.

options.name: global-namespace-index
options.brief: Use the global namespace page as an index for all symbols
options.details: When set to true, the page for the global namespace will recursively list all symbols in the documentation, not just those in the global namespace. This makes the global namespace page act as an index for the entire project.

options.name: stylesheets
options.brief: Ordered list of stylesheets to apply to HTML output
options.details: Ordered list of stylesheet names or paths. If empty, the bundled stylesheet is used. Entries can be local paths or remote URLs; remote URLs are only linked when `linkcss` is true. Inline mode embeds local styles; link mode emits `<link>` tags for each entry and copies local files.

options.name: no-default-styles
options.details: When set to true, the bundled stylesheet is not applied. Combine with an empty `stylesheets` list to emit no styles at all.

options.name: stylesdir
options.details: The directory MrDocs writes into the href of linked stylesheets when `linkcss` is true. Defaults to `css`. When local styles are copied, the directory is created under the output root, for example `css/mrdocs-default.css`.

options.name: linkcss
options.brief: Link stylesheets instead of embedding them
options.details: When set to true, stylesheets are linked with `<link>` tags instead of being inlined. Links use `stylesdir` plus the stylesheet name (e.g. `css/custom.css`). Local styles are copied unless `copycss` is false; remote URLs are linked as-is.

options.name: copycss
options.details: When `linkcss` is true, copy bundled and local stylesheet files into the output under `stylesdir`. Remote URLs are not copied. Set to false to skip copying.

details: These options control the diagnostics Mr.Docs emits as it runs: the warnings it reports about undocumented or malformed documentation, the logging verbosity and report file, the concurrency it uses, and how it behaves when it encounters errors.

options.name: verbose
options.details: When set to true, MrDocs prints extra information as it generates the documentation.

options.name: report
options.details: The reporting level determines the amount of information displayed during the generation of the documentation. The value `-1` delegates the decision to the `log-level` option.

options.name: log-level
options.details: The reporting level determines the amount of information displayed during the generation of the documentation.

options.name: warnings
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs warning messages during the generation of the documentation. It is usually recommended to enable warnings while writing the documentation.

options.name: warn-if-undocumented
options.brief: Warn if symbols are not documented
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs a warning message if a symbol that passes all filters is not documented.

options.name: warn-if-doc-error
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs a warning message if the documentation of a symbol has errors such as duplicate parameters and parameters that don't exist.

options.name: warn-no-paramdoc
options.brief: Warn if parameters are not documented
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs a warning message if a named function parameter is not documented.

options.name: warn-unnamed-param
options.brief: Warn if documented functions have unnamed parameters
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs a warning message if a documented function has a parameter that is not named.

options.name: warn-if-undoc-enum-val
options.brief: Warn if enum values are not documented
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs a warning message if an enum value is not documented.

options.name: warn-broken-ref
options.brief: Warn if a documentation reference is broken
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs outputs a warning message if a reference in the documentation is broken.

options.name: warn-as-error
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs treats warnings as errors and stops the generation of the documentation.

options.name: error-on-empty-corpus
options.brief: Treat an empty corpus as an error
options.details: When set to `true`, MrDocs treats an empty corpus as a hard error and exits with a failure status instead of emitting a warning and succeeding. A corpus counts as empty when no symbols are extracted; because the global namespace is always present in the model, a corpus that contains only the global namespace and no other declaration is also treated as empty. This usually means nothing was extracted, which is rarely intended in CI, so this turns that silent success into a detectable failure. This escalation applies regardless of the `warn-as-error` option.

options.name: concurrency
options.details: The desired level of concurrency: 0 for hardware-suggested.

options.name: ignore-map-errors
options.brief: Continue if files are not mapped correctly
options.details: When set to true, MrDocs continues to generate the documentation even if some files are not mapped correctly. Files are not mapped correctly when the source file is not found or the compilation database does not contain the compiler flags for the source file.

options.name: ignore-failures
options.brief: Whether AST visitation failures should not stop the program
options.details: When set to true, MrDocs continues to generate the documentation even if there are AST visitation failures. AST visitation failures occur when the source code contains constructs that are not supported by MrDocs.
